articles.title: 623 MW Power Deficit Likely During Peak Winters in Jammu Kashmir, Ladakh - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh are likely to witness a power deficiency of over 16 percent during the peak solar and non-solar hours in the month of December.
An official said that the regions may face power deficiency of nearly 16.3 percent during the peak solar and non-solar hours.
According to the official figures, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh is likely to face power paucity of 623 MWs against the available power position during the peak solar and non-solar hours in the month of December.
Stating the revised anticipated power supply position for December-2026 for both the Union Territories, the official said that there will likely be a peak availability of 3190 MW against the requirement of 3813 MW—keeping a loophole of 623 MW during the peak solar and non-solar hours.
Earlier this week, reports indicated that the onset of cold weather had pushed Kashmir into a daily power deficit of nearly 4,400 megawatt-hours (MWh), forcing consumers to endure scheduled power cuts amid falling temperatures.
An official had informed that “Over 24 hours, we face an actual power demand of 34,400 MWh. However, the power availability fluctuates from 29,000, 31000 MWh. There is a deficiency of nearly 4400 MWh.”
The official further said that on an average, there is a power deficiency of nearly 150 MW.
“On an average, we have a power availability of 1280 MW against a total requirement of 1435 MW,” he said.
HE further said, “Since yesterday, the peak power demand has increased by 50 MW. Till yesterday we were facing a peak non-solar power demand of 1650 MW which increased to 1700 MW today.”
As already reported, Hydro power generation in Jammu and Kashmir declines by nearly 80 percent.
An official had informed that the hydel power generation from the J&K owned projects was fluctuating between 250-280 Megawatt (MW).
“During the past week, the average power generation from the local generation projects was fluctuating from 250-280 or 270-300 MW,” the official said—(KNO)
